title: Paul McCartney buys Lower Gate Farm, Peasmarsh | 1979
content:
Paul and Linda McCartney purchased Lower Gate Farm in Peasmarsh, East Sussex, on 14 February 1979.

The property adjoined their 18th century home, Waterfall, which they had purchased for £40,000 in June 1974. It had 100 acres of fields and woodlands, as well as stables for their animals. The McCartneys made it their family home in 1975.

Lower Gate Farm had a farmhouse and gatehouse, and came with 60 acres of land. Paul and Linda immediately bought the property when it came up for sale, and completed the purchase within six weeks. They renamed the property Blossom Wood Farm.

Later in 1979, Paul McCartney commissioned Eddie Klein to install a studio at Blossom Wood Farm. Klein rented a 16-track Studer A-80 recording console and provided the additional equipment needed, including microphones, tape reels, and a 16-track mixing desk he had built. Paul first used it to record the McCartney II album.
